paper: APPSC Group-II Services Main Examination (Advt. No. 11/2023), Paper I: Social and Cultural History of Andhra Pradesh & Indian Constitution, held 23-02-2025 (Series A, 2G/201)

questions.s: Which one of the following statements is incorrect with reference to megalithic burials in Andhra ?
o: Tirupati has the largest anthropomorphic burial site collection
Many numbers of cyst burials were found in Vishakhapatnam District
Sarcophagus burials are more in number in Chittoor and Anantapuramu districts
Krishna and Chittoor districts contained many numbers of dolmen burials
questions.x: Cist burials in Andhra are concentrated in the southern and Rayalaseema/Krishna regions, not in Visakhapatnam district, so statement (2) is the incorrect one.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Statement (A) : "Gatha Saptasathi" is a collection of poems which predominantly focused on love and romantic themes.
Statement (B) : Gunadya had written Brihatkatha in Sanskrit language.
questions.x: Hala's Gatha Saptasati is a Prakrit anthology of mostly love poems, so (A) is true. Gunadhya wrote the Brihatkatha in Paisachi Prakrit, not Sanskrit, so (B) is false.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect with reference to the Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri ?
o: In their inscriptions, Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri had described themselves as the descendants of Ikshvakus of Ayodhya
Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri had matrimonial ties with Sakas/Western Satraps of Ujjain
Veerapurushadatta's reign is considered as the golden age of Buddhism in Andhra
questions.x: The Ikshvaku inscriptions of Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda) do not claim descent from the Ikshvakus of Ayodhya; that link was suggested by later scholars. The other three statements are accepted facts.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: 'Janasraya' is the title of which of the following Vishnukundin rulers ?
questions.x: Madhavavarma (II/III) of the Vishnukundins bore the title 'Janasraya'; the prosody work Janasrayi Chhandovichiti is associated with him.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Ayyana Mahadevi built the Jain temple 'Nedumba Vasati' near Vijayawada. She was the queen of
questions.x: Ayyana Mahadevi, queen of the Eastern Chalukya founder Kubja Vishnuvardhana, built the Nedumba Vasati at Bezawada (Vijayawada), as recorded in the Musinikonda grant.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler had transferred the capital from Amarapuri to Denduluru ?
questions.x: The initial key gave Madhavavarma, who is credited with moving the Vishnukundin capital to Denduluru near Eluru. APPSC's final key marks both (1) Vikramendravarma and (2) Madhavavarma as correct, so either scores.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : Trade with Rome flourished in the post-Satavahana era.
Reason (R) : No ruler had issued coins with ship motif after Satavahanas.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.x: Roman trade peaked in the Satavahana period and declined after it, so (A) is false. The ship-motif coins are characteristic of the Satavahanas (Yajnasri Satakarni) and were not issued by later rulers, so (R) is taken as true.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Which of the following statements is/are incorrect ?
a. Billa Surgam Palaeolithic cave site is located in Anantapuramu district.
b. Belum caves located in Nandyal district is the second longest cave in India.
c. Cave sites of Kurnool and Muchatla Chintamani Gavi in A.P. are the only places in India where tools made of animal bones were found in upper palaeolithic context.
questions.x: The Billa Surgam caves are in Kurnool (now Nandyal) district, not Anantapuramu, so only statement a is incorrect.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Which of the following statements is not true about the Satavahanas ?
o: They were described as Andhra Brithyas in Puranas
They issued bilingual coins in Prakrit and Dravidian Script
They were patrons of Buddhism and Hinduism
They had matrimonial alliance with Kakatiyas
questions.x: The Kakatiyas rose more than 800 years after the Satavahanas, so no marriage alliance between them was possible. The other statements are true.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Nannaya Bhattu are correct ?
I. Nannaya Bhattu was a Telugu poet and the author of 'Andhra Mahabharatam', a Telugu retelling of the Sanskrit-language Mahabharata.
II. He is also credited with writing the Andhra Shabda Chintamani, a Sanskrit treatise on Telugu grammar.
III. Raja Raja Narendra donated Nandampudi Agrahara to Nannaya.
questions.x: Nannaya began the Andhra Mahabharatam and is traditionally credited with the Sanskrit grammar Andhra Sabda Chintamani. The Nandampudi grant of Rajaraja Narendra was made to Narayana Bhatta, not to Nannaya, so III is wrong.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Which of the following statements is/are incorrect ?
I. Saktivarma had married Kundavai, the daughter of Raja Raja Chola I.
II. Raja Raja Narendra had married Ammangaidevi, the daughter of Rajendra Chola I.
III. Rajendra Chalukya had married Madurantaki, the daughter of Rajendra Chola II.
questions.x: Kundavai, daughter of Rajaraja Chola I, married Vimaladitya, not Saktivarma, so only statement I is incorrect.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are incorrect ?
a. Vijayaditya II is credited with the construction of 108 temples.
b. Raja Raja Narendra constructed Rajarajeswara temple at Biccavole.
c. Chalukya Bhima constructed Bhimeswara Swamy temple at Draksharama.
questions.x: The Rajarajeswara temple at Biccavole is attributed to Gunaga Vijayaditya III's period, not to Rajaraja Narendra, so only b is incorrect. Vijayaditya II is credited with 108 Siva temples and Chalukya Bhima I with the Draksharama Bhimeswara temple.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: The architectural structure of which of the following temples exemplifies the independent style of the Chalukya-Cholas, incorporating Pallava and early Chalukya influences ?
questions.x: The Bhimeswara temple at Draksharama shows the distinct Chalukya-Chola style that blends Pallava and early Chalukya elements.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Match List - I with List - II and select the correct answer from the codes given below. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Authors) / List - II (Works)
a. Ketana - I. Markandeya Puranam
b. Marana - II. Nirvachanottara Ramayanam
c. Tikkana - III. Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam
d. Manchena - IV. Keyurabahu Charitra
questions.x: Ketana wrote the grammar Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam, Marana the Markandeya Puranam, Tikkana the Nirvachanottara Ramayanam and Manchena the Keyurabahu Charitra.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Which of the following Chalukya-Chola Viceroys had assumed the title Sarvalokasraya, Sri Vishnuvardhana and celebrated his coronation at Jananathapura (Draksharama) ?
questions.x: Mummadi Chola, viceroy in Vengi, took the titles Sarvalokasraya Sri Vishnuvardhana and was crowned at Jananathapura (Draksharama).
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : Manumasiddhi II was reinstated on the throne by Ganapatideva.
Reason (R) : The power of Nellore Chodas was at its zenith during the reign of Manumasiddhi II.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.x: At Tikkana's request, the Kakatiya king Ganapatideva restored Manumasiddhi II to the Nellore throne, so (A) is true. The Nellore Chodas peaked under Tikka I, not Manumasiddhi II, so (R) is false.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Kakatiyas are correct ?
I. Early Kakatiya monarchs had constructed Jain temples.
II. The influence of Chalukya temple architecture could be seen in Kakatiya temples.
III. Thousand pillared temple was built in 'Trikuta style', having three shrines, each dedicated to Rudreshwara, Vasudeva and Suryadeva.
questions.x: Early Kakatiyas patronised Jainism, their temples follow the later Chalukya style, and the Thousand Pillar temple at Hanamkonda is a trikuta shrine to Rudreswara, Vasudeva and Surya. All three statements are correct.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Identify the wrong match.
(Author) - (Literary Work)
questions.x: Gangadevi wrote the Sanskrit Madhura Vijayam. Marichi Parinayam was written by Mohanangi, daughter of Krishnadevaraya, so pair (1) is the wrong match.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Arrange the following Reddi rulers chronologically :
A. Kumaragiri Reddi
B. Anavema Reddi
C. Anavota Reddi
D. Pedakomati Vema Reddi
questions.x: The Kondavidu Reddi line ran Prolaya Vema, Anavota, Anavema, Kumaragiri, then Pedakomati Vema, giving C, B, A, D.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Match List - I with List - II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Authors) / List - II (Works)
a. Pavuluri Mallana - I. Kreedabhiramam
b. Vinukonda Vallabharaya - II. Ganitasara Sangraham
c. Aryadeva - III. Chittasuddhi Prakarana
d. Dignaga - IV. Pramaana Samucchaya
questions.x: Pavuluri Mallana translated the mathematical Ganitasara Sangraham, Vinukonda Vallabharaya wrote Kreedabhiramam, Aryadeva wrote Chittavisuddhi Prakarana and Dignaga wrote Pramana Samuccaya.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Match List - I with List - II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Inscriptions) / List - II (Rulers)
a. Sanigaram inscription - I. Mailamba
b. Anumakonda inscription - II. Ganapatideva
c. Bayyaram inscription - III. Prolaraja
d. Motupalli inscription - IV. Rudradeva
questions.x: The Sanigaram inscription is of Prola, the Anumakonda (Thousand Pillar) inscription of Rudradeva, the Bayyaram tank inscription of Mailamba, and the Motupalli abhaya-sasana of Ganapatideva.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are incorrect ?
a. Prolaraja bore the title Arikesari.
b. Nayankara system was introduced by Prataparudra.
c. Beta II was initiated into Saivism by Rameswara Pandita of Srisailam.
questions.x: The key treats b as the only incorrect statement: the nayankara system is usually traced to earlier Kakatiya practice and was only expanded under Prataparudra. Statements a and c are accepted.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Which of the following books was not written by Srinatha ?
questions.x: Madana Vilasa Bhanam is a Sanskrit play by Vamana Bhatta Bana, not Srinatha. Haravilasam, Sivaratri Mahatmyam and Palnati Veera Charitra are Srinatha's works.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Sri Krishna Devaraya erected a pillar of victory to commemorate his conquest of coastal Andhra at
questions.x: After his Kalinga campaign, Krishnadevaraya set up a victory pillar (jayastambha) at Potnuru near Simhachalam.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Statement (A) : Moturpha is a salt tax levied by British East India Company.
Statement (B) : The revenue collected by the British East India Company from the zamindars is called 'Peshcush'.
questions.x: Moturpha was a tax on professions, trades and houses, not a salt tax, so (A) is false. The fixed tribute paid by zamindars to the Company was called peshkash, so (B) is true.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : Andhra region was not greatly affected by the 1857 revolt as Andhra had no local leaders.
Reason (R) : Then reigning Nizam, Nawab Afzal-ud-Dowla adopted pro-British attitude.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.x: The key treats both as true but unrelated: the coastal Andhra districts were under the Madras Presidency, so the Nizam's pro-British stance does not explain why Andhra stayed largely quiet.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect ?
o: Kandukuri Veeresalingam is known as the father of renaissance movement in Andhra
"The Crescent" is an English weekly founded by Mutnuri Krishna Rao
Andhra Patrika is the first Telugu political newsweekly
Krishna Patrika was started in 1902 by Konda Venkatappaya
questions.x: The Crescent (1844) was founded by Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty, not Mutnuri Krishna Rao, so (2) is incorrect. APPSC's final key also accepts (3), since the claim that Andhra Patrika was the first Telugu political newsweekly is disputed. Either (2) or (3) scores.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Match List - I with List - II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I / List - II
a. Kakinada riots case - I. February, 1909
b. Bipin Chandra Pal's tour in Andhra - II. July, 1907
c. Kotappa Konda riots - III. April, 1907
d. Tenali Bomb case - IV. April, 1909
questions.x: Bipin Chandra Pal toured Andhra in April 1907, the Kakinada riots followed in July 1907, the Kotappakonda riots took place in February 1909 and the Tenali bomb case in April 1909.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Eastern Ghats in Srikakulam are called
questions.x: The Eastern Ghats in Srikakulam district are known as the Mahendragiri hills; Papikondalu are on the Godavari and the Nallamalas and Palakondas are in Rayalaseema.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order :
A. Formation of the Visalandra Mahasabha
B. Dhar Commission
C. Swami Sitaram's fast
D. Formation of States Re-organization Commission
questions.x: The Dhar Commission reported in 1948, the Visalandhra Mahasabha formed in 1949, Swami Sitaram fasted in 1951 and the States Reorganisation Commission was set up in 1953.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : British ship 'Globe' under the command of Captain Hawkins arrived at Machilipatnam in 1611 A.D.
Reason (R) : Quli Qutub Shah permitted the English East India Company to establish a factory at Machilipatnam.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.x: The Globe reached Machilipatnam in 1611 under Captain Hippon, not Hawkins, so (A) is false. The Golconda Sultan (Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah) did allow the English to set up their factory there, so (R) is true.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Which of the following poets is known as "Abhinava Nannaya" ?
questions.x: The key marks Rayaprolu Subbarao, the pioneer of the Bhava Kavitvam movement, as the poet called 'Abhinava Nannaya'.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Which poet was called the "Poet of the Millennium" ?
questions.x: Gurram Jashuva was hailed as 'Navayuga Kavi Chakravarthi' and honoured as the poet of the millennium (Sahasrabdi Kavi) in Telugu.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect ?
o: September 28 marks the birth anniversary of Gurram Jashuva
He was presented the Sahitya Akademi award for his work titled 'Gabbilam' in 1964
He was appointed to the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council as a member in 1964
He was awarded the Padma Bhushan by the Government of India
questions.x: Jashuva won the Sahitya Akademi award in 1964 for 'Kreestu Charitra', not for 'Gabbilam', so statement (2) is incorrect.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam were known for their production of
questions.x: Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam on the Prakasam coast were well-known salt-producing centres and saw salt satyagraha activity in 1930.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Match List - I with List - II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Andhra Maha Sabha) / List - II (Presided by)
a. 1st Session Andhra Maha Sabha - I. Mocharla Ramachandra Rao
b. 2nd Session Andhra Maha Sabha - II. Nyapati Subba Rao
c. 3rd Session Andhra Maha Sabha - III. Baiya Narasimheswara Sharma
d. 4th Session Andhra Maha Sabha - IV. Raja Rama Rayanimgar
questions.x: The Andhra Mahasabha sessions from 1913 (Bapatla) were presided over in turn by B. N. Sarma, Nyapati Subba Rao, Panaganti Ramarayaningar and Mocharla Ramachandra Rao, which gives code (1).
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Arrange the following events chronologically :
A. Implementation of Ryotwari settlement in Madras.
B. Acquisition of Guntur by East India Company.
C. Battle of Padmanabham.
D. Abolition of Zamindari settlement in Andhra.
questions.x: The Company acquired Guntur in 1788, the Battle of Padmanabham was fought in 1794, Ryotwari was introduced in Madras around 1820 and zamindari was abolished by the 1948 Act.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Manchikallu and Maidavolu inscriptions belong to
questions.x: The Maidavolu plates of Sivaskandavarman and the Manchikallu inscription of Simhavarman are early Pallava Prakrit records found in Andhra.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Match List - I with List - II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Libraries) / List - II (Established in and at)
a. Vignana Chandrika Granthamandali - I. Kovvur, 1916
b. Srikrishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam - II. Hyderabad, 1906
c. Andhra Council of Research - III. Hyderabad, 1901
d. Andhra Saraswati Parishad - IV. Hyderabad, 1922
questions.x: Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was founded in Hyderabad in 1901 and the Vignana Chandrika Granthamandali in Hyderabad in 1906; the key pairs the Andhra Council of Research with Hyderabad 1922 and the Andhra Saraswati Parishad with Kovvur 1916.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Library Movement are correct ?
I. In 1915, the Andhra Desa Library Association started a periodical entitled 'Grandhalaya Sarvasvam' in Telugu.
II. Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao is the founder of "Andhra Patrika" established in 1908.
III. Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was established in Kovvur in 1916.
IV. In 1918, Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao started 'Boat Library Services' in West Godavari.
questions.x: Statement III is wrong because the Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was set up in Hyderabad in 1901. The other three statements are accepted as correct.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are incorrect ?
a. Communist Party leaders worked for the Visalandhra Movement and propagated the concept of Visalandhra even before the formation of Andhra State.
b. Communists became a great force in Telangana politics.
c. Communists opposed the formation of integrated linguistic States.
questions.x: The Communists were the main champions of Visalandhra and of linguistic states, so c is the only incorrect statement.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Who was the Chairman of the Partition Committee constituted by Madras State Government for the formation of separate State ?
questions.x: The 1949 Partition Committee of the Madras Government was chaired by Chief Minister P. S. Kumaraswamy Raja.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Arrange the following ex-Chief Ministers of Andhra Pradesh chronologically and choose the correct answer :
A. Tanguturi Anjaiah
B. Damodaram Sanjivaiah
C. P. V. Narasimha Rao
D. Kasu Brahmananda Reddy
questions.x: Sanjivaiah was Chief Minister in 1960-62, Brahmananda Reddy in 1964-71, P. V. Narasimha Rao in 1971-73 and Anjaiah in 1980-82.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: According to the Gentlemen's Agreement, what was the ratio of Cabinet representation for Andhra and Telangana ?
questions.x: The 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement fixed Cabinet posts at 60 per cent for Andhra and 40 per cent for Telangana.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Who was the first Telugu writer to win Jnanapith Award for the work titled "Ramayana Kalpavriksham" ?
questions.x: Viswanatha Satyanarayana received the Jnanpith Award in 1970 for Ramayana Kalpavrukshamu, the first for a Telugu writer.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: In which year was the English East India Company established ?
questions.x: The English East India Company received its royal charter from Elizabeth I on 31 December 1600.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Which of the following Parties wanted Tirupati as the Capital of Andhra in 1953 ?
questions.x: During the 1953 capital debate the Krishikar Lok Party, strong in Rayalaseema, pressed for Tirupati as the capital of the new Andhra State.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Match List - I with List - II and select the correct answer using the codes given below. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Salt Satyagrahis) / List - II (Broke Salt Laws at)
a. Bulusu Sambamurty - I. Kakinada
b. Dandu Narayana Raju - II. Mattapalem
c. Kasi Viswanadham - III. Vadarevu
d. Pattabhi Sitaramayya - IV. Masulipatnam
questions.x: In the 1930 salt satyagraha Bulusu Sambamurti led at Kakinada, Dandu Narayana Raju at Mattapalem, Kasi Viswanadham at Vadarevu and Pattabhi Sitaramayya at Machilipatnam.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Where was the French Settlement in Andhra ?
questions.x: Yanam on the Godavari delta was a French settlement until 1954 and is now part of Puducherry.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: The inscriptions of early Satavahana kings were found in
questions.x: The earliest Satavahana records, such as the Naneghat inscription of Naganika and the Nasik cave inscriptions, are in Maharashtra.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Justice Party Government helped the formation of which University ?
questions.x: Andhra University was set up in 1926 under the Justice Party ministry of the Madras Presidency.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: In which book was the song 'Desamante Matti Kadoi' written ?
questions.x: Gurajada Apparao's patriotic song 'Desamante matti kadoyi, desamante manushuloy' is part of his collection Mutyala Saralu.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Match Group - A with Group - B and select the correct answer using the codes given below. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
Group - A / Group - B
a. Jainism - i. Nature Worship
b. Buddhism - ii. Ashtanga Margam
c. Saivism - iii. Triratna
d. Animism - iv. Linga
questions.x: Triratna (three jewels) is the core of Jainism, the eightfold (ashtanga) path belongs to Buddhism, the linga is the symbol of Saivism and animism is nature worship.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Match Group - A with Group - B and select the correct answer using the codes given below. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
Group - A / Group - B
a. Duggirala Gopala Krishnaiah - i. Pedanandipadu agitation
b. Parvataneni Veeraiah Choudary - ii. Najeevitha Katha
c. Ayyadevara Kaleswar Rao - iii. Rama Dandu
d. Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Choudary - iv. Kavi Raju
questions.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya organised the Rama Dandu volunteers, Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary led the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign, Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao wrote the autobiography Naa Jeevitha Katha and Tripuraneni Ramaswamy was called Kaviraju.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s:
Match Group - A with Group - B and select the correct answer using the codes given below. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
Group - A (Book) / Group - B (Author)
a. Japaneeyamu - i. Gurajada Appa Rao
b. Mahaprasthanam - ii. Sri Sri
c. Kanyasulkam - iii. Puchalapalli Sundarayya
d. Veyipadagalu - iv. Viswanadha Satyanarayana
v. Sriram Veerabrahmam
questions.x: Japaneeyamu is a travelogue by Sriram Veerabrahmam, Mahaprasthanam is by Sri Sri, Kanyasulkam by Gurajada Apparao and Veyipadagalu by Viswanatha Satyanarayana.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Which religion did King Kharavela patronise ?
questions.x: The Hathigumpha inscription shows Kharavela of Kalinga as a devoted patron of Jainism who built caves for Jain monks at Udayagiri.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Undavally caves are associated with
questions.x: The rock-cut Undavalli caves near Vijayawada are attributed to the Vishnukundin rulers of the 4th-5th centuries.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Blue Water Policy is associated with
questions.x: The Blue Water Policy of controlling the seas rather than land was adopted by the Portuguese viceroy Francisco de Almeida.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Who was known as the first Principal Collector of Rayalaseema ?
questions.x: Thomas Munro was appointed the first Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts (Rayalaseema) in 1800.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: The first Telugu to English dictionary was composed by
questions.x: Charles Philip Brown compiled the Telugu-English dictionary published in 1852, one of his many services to Telugu.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Which was the First Telugu Newspaper ?
questions.x: APPSC's final key marks Krishna Patrika (1902, Machilipatnam). The key is debatable, because the missionary monthly Satyadoota (1835) is often called the first Telugu periodical.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Where did the English establish their first factory in Coastal Andhra ?
questions.x: The English set up their first factory on the east coast at Machilipatnam in 1611.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: The Padmanabha battle was fought between
questions.x: At Padmanabham in 1794 the East India Company's forces defeated and killed Vijayarama Raju II of Vizianagaram.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Who was the last Asaf Jahi (Nizam) ruler ?
questions.x: Mir Osman Ali Khan, the seventh Nizam, was the last Asaf Jahi ruler of Hyderabad State.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Who was the founder of Vivekavardhini Newspaper ?
questions.x: Kandukuri Veeresalingam started the reformist journal Viveka Vardhini in 1874.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: The first novel in Telugu language was
questions.x: Veeresalingam's Rajasekhara Charitram (1878) is regarded as the first Telugu novel.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Who was the author of "Veera Telangana Anubhavalu Gnapakalu" ?
questions.x: The key credits Ravi Narayana Reddy, a leader of the Telangana armed struggle, with the memoir 'Veera Telangana Anubhavalu Gnapakalu'.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Andhra State was formed on
questions.x: Andhra State was carved out of Madras State on 1 October 1953 with Kurnool as its capital.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Who was the founder of the first girls schools at Rajahmundry ?
questions.x: Kandukuri Veeresalingam opened a girls' school at Dowlaiswaram/Rajahmundry in 1874 as part of his women's education work.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Who was the leader of Chirala Perala Movement ?
questions.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya led the people of Chirala-Perala in their 1919-21 protest against the municipal tax, moving them out of the town.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: "No Pullari (Grass) Tax" Movement was led in Palanadu by
questions.x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu led the Palnadu forest satyagraha against the pullari (grazing) tax in 1921-22.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Telugu Ganga Canal Water is supplied to which of the following states ?
questions.x: The Telugu Ganga project carries Krishna water through Andhra Pradesh to supply drinking water to Chennai in Tamil Nadu.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Who was the founder of Andhra Bank ?
questions.x: Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya founded Andhra Bank at Machilipatnam in 1923.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Which Fruit was introduced by the Portuguese to the Telugu soil ?
questions.x: The tomato is a New World crop that reached India through the Portuguese.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Who was the founder of Common Weal and New India newspapers ?
questions.x: Annie Besant started the weekly Commonweal and took over the Madras Standard, renaming it New India, in 1914.
questions.subject: Social & Cultural History of AP

questions.s: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution on the recommendations of
questions.x: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended Fundamental Duties, which the 42nd Amendment added as Article 51A.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: The term "Secular" was added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by
questions.x: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 inserted the words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' into the Preamble.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Match List - I with List - II. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Borrowed Feature) / List - II (Source)
a. Emergency Provisions - i. United Kingdom
b. Suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency - ii. Australia
c. Concept of Concurrent List - iii. Government of India Act, 1935
d. Single Citizenship - iv. German Constitution
v. USA
questions.x: Emergency provisions come from the Government of India Act 1935, suspension of rights during emergency from the Weimar (German) Constitution, the Concurrent List from Australia and single citizenship from the UK.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Which of the following statements are true regarding 97th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2011 ?
A. Gave Constitutional status and protection to Co-operative Societies.
B. Made the right to form Co-operative Societies a Fundamental Right under Article 19.
C. It added a new Part X-B to the Constitution.
D. Added new Directive Principle under Article 43-B.
Choose the right answer from the codes given below :
questions.x: The 97th Amendment gave co-operatives constitutional status, added the right to form them to Article 19(1)(c) and inserted Article 43B, but the new part it added was Part IXB, not X-B.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: Which Article of the Indian Constitution is described as the "heart and soul" of the Constitution by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar ?
questions.x: Ambedkar called Article 32, the right to constitutional remedies, the very soul and heart of the Constitution.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: Indian Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly of India on
questions.x: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949; it came fully into force on 26 January 1950.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: Which part of the Indian Constitution deals with the Union Executive ?
questions.x: Part V (Articles 52-151) deals with the Union, including the President, Vice-President and Council of Ministers.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: How many Schedules were there in the original Indian Constitution ?
questions.x: The Constitution as adopted in 1949 had eight Schedules; four more were added later, making twelve.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: When was the Human Rights Commission of India constituted ?
questions.x: The National Human Rights Commission was set up on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Ordinance, later the 1993 Act.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Match List - I with List - II. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (National Commission) / List - II (Name of First Chairperson)
a. National Commission for STs - i. Justice R. N. Prasad
b. National Commission for Minorities - ii. Kunwar Singh
c. National Commission for SCs - iii. Justice Mohammad Sardar Ali Khan
d. National Commission for BCs - iv. Suraj Bhan
questions.x: The first chairpersons were Kunwar Singh Tekam (STs, 2004), Justice Mohammad Sardar Ali Khan (Minorities, 1993), Suraj Bhan (SCs, 2004) and Justice R. N. Prasad (BCs, 1993).
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct ?
A. Residuary powers of legislation are included in Article 248 of the Constitution of India.
B. The Union Parliament has exclusive powers over any item not covered in the State or Concurrent Lists.
questions.x: Article 248 gives Parliament exclusive power to legislate on any matter not listed in the State or Concurrent Lists, so both statements are correct.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Match List - I with List - II. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Writ) / List - II (Meaning)
a. Quo-Warranto - i. to be certified
b. Mandamus - ii. by what Authority
c. Habeas Corpus - iii. we command
d. Certiorari - iv. to have the body of
questions.x: Quo warranto means 'by what authority', mandamus 'we command', habeas corpus 'to have the body' and certiorari 'to be certified'.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: The concept of Judicial Activism was originated and developed in
questions.x: Judicial activism and judicial review grew out of the US Supreme Court's practice, beginning with Marbury v. Madison (1803).
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: The State Election Commission conducts elections to
questions.x: Under Articles 243K and 243ZA the State Election Commission conducts elections to panchayats and municipalities; legislature elections are run by the Election Commission of India.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Arrange the following Committees of Panchayat Raj in chronological order.
a. Gadgil Committee
b. Dantwala Committee
c. L. M. Singhvi Committee
d. Balwant Rai Mehta Committee
questions.x: Balwant Rai Mehta reported in 1957, Dantwala in 1978, L. M. Singhvi in 1986 and the Gadgil Committee in 1988.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 came into force on
questions.x: The 74th Amendment on urban local bodies came into force on 1 June 1993; the 73rd came into force on 24 April 1993.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct ?
A. The Cantonments Act was passed by the Central Legislature in 1924.
B. The first municipal corporation came into existence at Madras in 1688.
C. Lord Rippon is regarded as the Father of Local Self Government in India.
questions.x: The Cantonments Act was passed in 1924, the Madras Municipal Corporation was set up in 1688 and Lord Ripon's 1882 resolution earned him the title Father of Local Self-Government, so all three are correct.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Which of the following statements is/are not true regarding Electronic Voting Machines (EVM) ?
A. EVMs were used for the first time in the entire State of Goa in the general elections to the Assembly in 1999.
B. EVMs were used for the first time on experimental basis in the selected constituencies in the Assembly elections to the States of Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat in 1998.
o: Both A and B are true
questions.x: Goa did use EVMs statewide in its 1999 Assembly election. The 1998 experimental use covered Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi, not Gujarat, so only B is untrue.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: Which of the following Constitution Amendment Acts reduced the minimum age for voting from 21 to 18 years ?
questions.x: The 61st Amendment Act, 1988 amended Article 326 to lower the voting age from 21 to 18.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Match List - I with List - II. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Committee) / List - II (Related Electoral Reform)
a. Vohra Committee - i. Amendments to Criminal Law
b. Indrajit Gupta Committee - ii. Electoral Disqualifications
c. Dinesh Goswami Committee - iii. State funding of elections
d. J. S. Varma Committee - iv. Electoral reforms
v. Nexus between crime and politics
questions.x: The Vohra Committee studied the criminal-political nexus, Indrajit Gupta state funding of elections, Dinesh Goswami electoral reforms, and the J. S. Verma Committee amendments to criminal law.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true relating to Election Commission of India ?
A. The Election Commission of India is a three member Body.
B. The Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India.
C. Election Commission of India is a Constitutional Body.
questions.x: The ECI is a constitutional body under Article 324 and currently has three members, but the CEC is appointed by the President, not the Chief Justice.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
In the list given below, how many are Constitutional Bodies ?
a. NITI Aayog
b. National Commission for Minorities
c. Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
d. National Human Rights Commission
questions.x: Only the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (Article 350B) is constitutional. NITI Aayog is an executive body, and the NCM and NHRC are statutory.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: As per 91st Amendment Act of 2003, the total number of ministers including the Prime Minister, in the Central Council of Ministers shall not exceed ________ of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
questions.x: Article 75(1A), inserted by the 91st Amendment, caps the Union Council of Ministers at 15 per cent of the Lok Sabha's strength.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: Who described Indian Union as, "a federation with a centralising tendency" ?
questions.x: Sir Ivor Jennings described India as a federation with a strong centralising tendency, while K. C. Wheare called it quasi-federal.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: The power to increase the number of judges in the Supreme Court of India is vested in
questions.x: Under Article 124(1) Parliament can increase the number of Supreme Court judges by law, through the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Arrange the following political parties in the chronological order of their establishment.
A. Samaj Wadi Party
B. Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam
C. Bahujan Samaj Party
D. Telugu Desam Party
questions.x: The DMK was founded in 1949, the TDP in 1982, the BSP in 1984 and the Samajwadi Party in 1992.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
As per the provisions of Right to Information Act, the State Chief Information Commissioner is appointed by the Governor, on the recommendations of a committee comprising of,
A. Chief Minister of the concerned State
B. Chief Justice of the concerned State High Court
C. Leader of the Opposition in the State Assembly
D. Cabinet Minister nominated by the Chief Minister
questions.x: Section 15(3) of the RTI Act names the Chief Minister, the Leader of Opposition and a Cabinet Minister nominated by the CM; the High Court Chief Justice is not a member.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Which of the following violate the federal principles of the Indian Constitution ?
A. Office of the Governor
B. Central Services
C. Office of the Comptroller and Auditor General
D. Emergency Powers
questions.x: The key treats the Centre-appointed Governor, a single CAG auditing both Union and State accounts, and the emergency powers as departures from federal principles; Central (All India) Services are not counted.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Match List - I with List - II. (Common code for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Subject) / List - II (List)
a. Organisation of High Courts - i. Concurrent List
b. Taxes on Mineral Rights - ii. Union List
c. Education - iii. State List
questions.x: Constitution and organisation of High Courts is Union List entry 78, taxes on mineral rights is State List entry 50, and education has been in the Concurrent List since 1976.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: By which of the following Acts, the Governor General of Bengal was designated as the Governor General of India ?
questions.x: The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India; Lord William Bentinck was the first to hold the title.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: When did The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 come into force ?
questions.x: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act received assent on 1 January 2014 and came into force on 16 January 2014.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
The Parliament can make laws on subjects enumerated in the State list in the following conditions
A. On the request of two or more States.
B. The Rajya Sabha passes a resolution with at least two-thirds of the members present and voting, authorizing the Parliament to make laws on the subject in the national interest.
C. Proclamation of International Agreements.
D. The Lok Sabha passes a resolution with at least two-thirds of the members present and voting, authorizing the Parliament to make laws on the subject in the national interest.
questions.x: Parliament can legislate on State subjects at the request of two or more States (Art. 252), on a Rajya Sabha resolution (Art. 249) and to implement international agreements (Art. 253). A Lok Sabha resolution has no such effect.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: The 11th Fundamental Duty was added by which Constitutional Amendment Act ?
questions.x: The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added Article 51A(k), the duty of parents to provide education to children aged 6-14.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : The UPSC is the Central recruiting agency in India.
Reason (R) : It is an independent recruiting constitutional body.
o: Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is not a correct explanation of (A)
questions.x: The UPSC is India's central recruiting agency and is an independent constitutional body under Article 315, but its constitutional status does not explain why it is the recruiting agency.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act is a significant landmark in the evolution of grassroots democratic institutions in the country.
Reason (R) : This Act has brought the Panchayath Raj institutions under the purview of justiciable part of the Constitution.
o: Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.x: The 73rd Amendment moved panchayats from the non-justiciable Directive Principles (Article 40) into the justiciable Part IX, giving them constitutional status. That is why it is a landmark.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : The All India Services violate the federal principle of the Constitution as well as the autonomy of States.
Reason (R) : The All India Service officers are governed by Central Government rules and the State Governments do not have full control over them.
o: Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.x: All India Service officers serve the States but are recruited and disciplined under central rules, so States lack full control over them. That is the basis of the criticism that these services dilute federalism.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : NITI Aayog is a Non-Constitutional Advisory Body.
Reason (R) : One of the objectives of NITI Aayog is to develop mechanisms to formulate credible plans at the village level and aggregate these progressively at higher levels of government.
o: Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are True but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.x: NITI Aayog was created by an executive resolution in 2015, and bottom-up village-level planning is one of its stated objectives. That objective does not explain why it is non-constitutional.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : Article 263 contemplates the establishment of an Inter-State Council to effect co-ordination between the States and between Center and the States.
Reason (R) : Rajmannar Committee made a strong case for establishment of the Inter-State Council.
o: Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are True but (R) is not a correct explanation of (A)
questions.x: Article 263 provides for an Inter-State Council, and the Rajamannar Committee (1969) did urge setting one up. The committee's recommendation came long after the Article and does not explain it.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Which of the following will be the correct consequences of declaration of National Emergency by the President ?
A. The President can modify the constitutional distribution of finances between the Center and the States.
B. The Center becomes entitled to give executive directions to a State on any matter.
C. The President can suspend all the Fundamental Rights of the citizens.
questions.x: During a national emergency the President can modify revenue sharing (Art. 354) and the Centre can direct States on any matter (Art. 353). Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended, so C is wrong.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Which of the following statements are correct ?
A. Public Interest Litigation (PIL) is also known as Social Action Litigation.
B. PIL is an outcome of Judicial Restraint.
C. Justice V. R. Krishna Iyer and Justice P. N. Bhagawathi were pioneers of the concept of PIL.
questions.x: PIL is also called social action litigation and was pioneered by Justices Krishna Iyer and Bhagwati. It grew out of judicial activism, not judicial restraint, so B is wrong.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: Which of the following is not on Center - State Relations ?
questions.x: The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) dealt with state funding of elections. Sarkaria, Rajamannar and Punchhi all examined Centre-State relations.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: Which of the following is not a condition for the political party to be recognised as National Party ?
o: The party wins two percent of seats in the Lok Sabha from at least three different states

The party, at a general election to Lok Sabha or Legislative Assembly, polls six percent of valid votes in any four or more States and in addition it wins four Lok Sabha seats from any State or States
It is recognised as a State party in any four States
questions.x: Each of the three listed conditions is one of the alternative criteria under the Election Symbols Order for national party status, so 'None of the above' is correct.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Which of the following statements is/are not correct regarding the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act ?
A. 18 functional items were placed within the purview of Panchayats.
B. The Act does not apply to the States of Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram.
C. The Act bars interference by courts in the electoral matters of Panchayats.
D. Reservation of seats to BCs is a compulsory provision under this Act.
questions.x: The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects, not 18, and reservation for backward classes is left to the States. B and C are correct provisions (Articles 243M and 243O).
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
The President is elected by an Electoral College consisting of
A. Elected members of both Houses of Parliament.
B. Nominated members of both Houses of Parliament.
C. The elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of all the States.
D. Nominated members of the Legislative Assemblies of all the States.
E. The elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of NCT of Delhi and the Union Territory of Puducherry.
o: A, B, C, D and E
questions.x: Under Article 54 the electoral college has only elected members of Parliament, the State Assemblies and the Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry; nominated members do not vote.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts was declared unconstitutional and void by the Supreme Court in 2015 ?
questions.x: In the Fourth Judges case (October 2015) the Supreme Court struck down the 99th Amendment, which had created the National Judicial Appointments Commission.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Match List - I with List - II and choose the right answer from the codes given below. (Common code for English and Telugu Versions) :
List - I / List - II
a. Separate representation of the Muslim Community - i. Government of India Act, 1935
b. Dyarchy in the provinces - ii. Indian Councils Act, 1892
c. Prescribed Federation - iii. Indian Councils Act, 1909
d. Discussion of Annual Statement - iv. Indian Councils Act, 1861
v. Government of India Act, 1919
questions.x: Separate electorates for Muslims came with the 1909 Act, provincial dyarchy with the 1919 Act and the proposed All-India Federation with the 1935 Act. The 1892 Act allowed discussion of the annual financial statement.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding Finance Commission ?
o: Finance Commission is a Quasi-judicial Body
Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and four other members
Article 290 provides for the Constitution of Finance Commission
questions.x: The Finance Commission is set up under Article 280. Article 290 deals with adjustment of certain expenses and pensions.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: Which of the following objectives is not embodied in the Preamble to the Constitution of India ?
questions.x: The Preamble promises liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship, and political justice. 'Political liberty' is not among its words.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Which of the following statements about the Attorney General of India is/are correct ?
i. The President shall appoint a person who is qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court to be Attorney General of India.
ii. He shall have right of audience in all courts in the territory of India.
iii. He shall hold office during the pleasure of the Prime Minister.
iv. He shall receive remuneration as the Parliament may determine.
questions.x: Under Article 76 the AG must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge and has right of audience in all courts. He holds office at the pleasure of the President, not the PM, and his remuneration is fixed by the President, not Parliament.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Match the Constitutions of different countries given in List - A with their Provisions given in List - B which are adopted in Indian Constitution. (Common code for English and Telugu Versions)
List - A / List - B
a. UK Constitution - i. The idea of Residual Powers
b. Irish Constitution - ii. The idea of Rule of Law
c. United States of America Constitution - iii. Directive Principles of State Policy
d. Canadian Constitution - iv. Power of Judicial Review
questions.x: India took the rule of law from the UK, the Directive Principles from Ireland, judicial review from the USA and the vesting of residuary powers in the Centre from Canada.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Which of the following statements are correct about Presidential system ?
i. President is head of the State.
ii. President is head of the Government.
iii. President is directly elected by the people.
iv. President is accountable to legislature.
o: Only i, ii and iv are correct
Only i and iii are correct
Only i, ii and iii are correct
Only ii and iv are correct
questions.x: In a presidential system the President is both head of state and head of government and is elected by the people for a fixed term. He is not accountable to the legislature.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Which of the following statements about State Finance Commission is/are correct ?
i. This Commission examines the financial position of the local governments in the State.
ii. It also reviews the distribution of revenues between the State and Local governments on the one hand and between rural and urban local governments on the other.
questions.x: Under Articles 243-I and 243Y the State Finance Commission reviews the finances of panchayats and municipalities and recommends how revenues should be shared, so both statements are correct.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Which of the following statements about the Vice President of India are correct ?
i. The Vice President is elected for five years.
ii. The Vice President acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
iii. The Vice President acts as the President only until a new President is elected.
questions.x: The Vice President has a five-year term, is ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and, in a vacancy, acts as President only until a new President is elected.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: In which of the following hours, members of the Parliament are free to raise any matter that they think is important ?
questions.x: Zero Hour is an informal Indian practice in which members raise urgent matters without prior notice; Question Hour is limited to questions admitted in advance.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: The most powerful weapon that enables the Parliament to ensure executive accountability is
questions.x: A no-confidence motion can remove the Council of Ministers, which is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha under Article 75(3), so it is the strongest accountability tool.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Correctly match the following in List - A with List - B. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - A / List - B
a. Art. 137 - i. Restoring Fundamental Rights by Supreme Court by issuing writs.
b. Art. 226 - ii. Power of Supreme Court to review any judgment pronounced or Order made by it.
c. Art. 13 - iii. The High Courts also have the power to issue Writs for protecting Fundamental Rights.
d. Art. 32 - iv. Supreme Court can declare the concerned law as unconstitutional.
questions.x: Article 137 lets the Supreme Court review its own judgments, Article 226 gives High Courts writ powers, Article 13 voids laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights, and Article 32 lets the Supreme Court enforce them by writs.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act came into effect on
questions.x: The J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 took effect on 31 October 2019, creating the Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : Right to Property is made a legal right under Article 300-A in Part XII of the Constitution.
Reason (R) : 44th Amendment Act of 1978 eliminated the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.x: The 44th Amendment deleted Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 from the Fundamental Rights and, in their place, made property a constitutional (legal) right under Article 300A.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: Regarding the Panchayat Raj System, in 1978 Ashok Mehta Committee recommended for
o: two tier system with four years of term
three tier system with four years of term
two tier system with five years of term
three tier system with six years of term
questions.x: The Ashok Mehta Committee recommended a two-tier system of Zilla Parishad and Mandal Panchayat with a four-year term.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Of the following, which are the appointments made by the President on the recommendation of the Prime Minister ?
i. Chief Justice of India
ii. Judges of Supreme Court and High Courts
iii. Attorney General of India
iv. Governors of States
questions.x: The key treats all four as formal appointments made by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers under Article 74.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Which of the following provisions of 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act related to Panchayat Raj Institutions is/are correct ?
i. The members of these bodies are directly elected by the people.
ii. Elections shall be held within a period of 3 months from the dissolution of the body.
iii. Women have been given 1/3rd reservation in Panchayats.
iv. The minimum age required to become member is 21 years.
questions.x: Article 243E requires fresh elections within six months of dissolution, not three, so ii is wrong. Direct election, one-third reservation for women and the minimum age of 21 are correct.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Consider the following statements :
Assertion (A) : One of the most controversial Articles in the Constitution is Article 356.
Reason (R) : It is imposed when the Government of the State cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.x: Article 356 (President's Rule) applies when a State's government cannot be carried on according to the Constitution. That broad, subjective ground is why it has been so often misused and so controversial.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : Mandamus normally is not issued to Govt. for making law.
Reason (R) : Mandamus cannot lie in absence of policy. Once policy is laid down, terms of policy can be enforced.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.x: Courts do not issue mandamus directing the government to legislate or frame policy; mandamus can only enforce a duty under an existing law or policy. That is why (R) explains (A).
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : Directive Principles of State Policy are not capable of being independently enforced in a Court of Law.
Reason (R) : They act as guide post for legislation.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.x: Article 37 makes the Directive Principles non-justiciable yet fundamental in governance, and they guide legislation. In its final key APPSC changed the answer from (1) to (2): both statements are true, but serving as a guide for legislation is not why they are unenforceable.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Are the statements given below in the Indian Constitution ?
Statement (A) : Ownership and control of the material resources of the community are so distributed as best to subserve the common good.
Statement (B) : Operation of the economic system does not result in the concentration of wealth and means of production to the common detriment.
o: Both Statements (A) and (B) are not there
questions.x: Both statements are in the Constitution, as Article 39(b) and Article 39(c) of the Directive Principles.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Directive Principles of State Policy contain which of the following ?
a. Free Legal Aid
b. Maternity Relief
c. Living Wage
d. Safeguarding of Forests
e. Protection of Monuments
o: a, b, c, d and e
questions.x: Free legal aid (39A), maternity relief (42), living wage (43), protecting forests (48A) and protecting monuments (49) are all Directive Principles.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: Panchayats have responsibilities in respect of which of the following as per the Eleventh Schedule ?
questions.x: Libraries are item 20 of the Eleventh Schedule. Slaughter houses, regulation of land use and burial grounds are Twelfth Schedule (municipal) items.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: Municipalities have Constitutional responsibilities in respect of which of the following as per the Twelfth Schedule ?
questions.x: Cattle pounds and prevention of cruelty to animals are in the Twelfth Schedule. The other three options are Eleventh Schedule (panchayat) items.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Statement (A) : There is no fundamental right to marry.
Statement (B) : Right to travel abroad comes under the purview of Fundamental Rights.
o: Statement (A) is right and Statement (B) is wrong
Statement (A) is wrong and Statement (B) is right
questions.x: APPSC's key accepts (A), since there is no separately listed fundamental right to marry. Since Maneka Gandhi (1978), the right to travel abroad is part of personal liberty under Article 21, so (B) is right too.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s: Which of the following is not a Fundamental Duty as mentioned in the Constitution ?
o: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
To value and preserve the rich heritage of the country's composite culture
To protect the elderly, differently abled and children
To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood
questions.x: Article 51A has no duty to protect the elderly and differently abled; the other three are listed duties.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct ?
i. Under Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act (RPA) 1951, no election can be called in question except by an election petition presented in accordance with the provisions of this part.
ii. Only the High Courts have original jurisdiction on deciding on election petitions.
iii. An election petition calling in question an election shall be filed within the time period of 30 days from the date of declaration of results.
questions.x: The bar on challenging elections except by petition is in Section 80 of the RPA, not Section 81, and petitions must be filed within 45 days, not 30. Election petitions are tried by the High Court, so only ii is correct.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
With reference to the Indian Judiciary, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct ?
i. Any retired judge of the Supreme Court of India can be called back to sit and act as a Supreme Court Judge by the Chief Justice of India with the prior permission of the President of India.
ii. A High Court in India has the power to review its own Judgement as the Supreme Court does although there has been no specific power of review conferred on it by the Constitution.
questions.x: Article 128 lets the CJI, with the President's prior consent, ask a retired Supreme Court judge to sit again. As courts of record, High Courts also have an inherent power to review their own judgments. In its final key APPSC changed the answer from (1) to (3).
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Assertion (A) : The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976) is known as 'Mini-Constitution'.
Reason (R) : The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976) made changes to the Preamble, the Seventh Schedule and to 54 Articles of the Constitution.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation for (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation for (A)
questions.x: The 42nd Amendment is widely called the 'mini-Constitution' because of how much it changed. APPSC's key treats (R) as false because its description of the extent of the changes (54 Articles) is not accurate.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the administration of tribal areas under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution is/are correct ?
i. It is applicable in all States where Scheduled Tribes make up more than 40% of the State's population.
ii. These areas are outside the authority of the State Legislature as well as State Executive.
iii. Only the President can organise and reorganise the autonomous districts in these areas.
iv. The High Court of the State does not have any jurisdiction in these areas.
questions.x: The Sixth Schedule applies only to tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. The Governor, not the President, organises autonomous districts, and the State's executive and High Court still have jurisdiction. All four statements are wrong.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct ?
i. Floating Constituencies are the constituencies without fixed geographical borders.
ii. In the constituency of Sangha in Sikkim, only Buddhist monks can contest and vote.
questions.x: Sikkim's Sangha seat is a non-territorial ('floating') constituency with no fixed boundaries, in which only registered lamas and monks of the Buddhist monasteries can stand and vote. Both statements are correct.
questions.subject: Indian Constitution
